spec-ranked for two nights, not a week
sources.evidence: A 5kWh unit runs a CPAP for a week, but nobody needs a 145 lb battery beside the bed.

sources.why: nights per dollar, humidifier figures from ResMed, camping pick
sources.evidence: ResMed's figures are about 28 W with the heated humidifier and 11 W without, so the same battery lasts about 2.5 times longer.

sources.why: arithmetic table, no AirSense 11 or week focus
sources.evidence: Runtime is battery size times 0.85 (about 15% is lost turning battery power into wall power), divided by the draw.
Turning off the heated humidifier and heated tubing is the single biggest way to stretch runtime.
Van life, a week or more, or CPAP plus a fridge: 1000Wh with a 500W solar input, so the battery refills itself while you are out during the day.

sources.why: one unit focus, home outage emphasis
sources.evidence: Many CPAP users buy their first power station for exactly this and never take it camping.

sources.why: generic spec table, mostly out of stock
sources.evidence: Running it from a DC outlet instead of AC skips the inverter and stretches runtime by roughly 8%.
EcoFlow Delta 2 review for camping : r/CPAP

sources.why: covers week trip, DC vs AC, humidifier, weight
sources.evidence: With the humidifier off and the ResMed DC converter, a 768 Wh station is good for a week-long trip on paper (12 nights best case).
turning the heated humidifier on can roughly halve your runtime, and running the CPAP off a 12V DC cable instead of the AC outlet gets you ~15–30% more.
